content: Brompheniramine is an antihistamine medication that is used to alleviate symptoms such as red, irritated, itchy, and watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny nose caused by allergies, hay fever, or the common cold. It can also help relieve itching caused by insect bites, bee stings, poison ivy, and poison oak. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in several forms, including regular tablets, extended-release tablets, and liquid formulations, all of which are taken orally. The dosing schedule typically ranges from every 4, 6, 8, or 12 hours, depending on the specific needs of the patient. It is crucial to follow the instructions provided on the package label or prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Brompheniramine should be taken exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. Extended-release tablets must be swallowed whole and should not be crushed, broken, or chewed. These tablets are not suitable for children under 12 years of age, and regular tablets or liquid formulations should not be given to children under 6 years of age unless specifically instructed by a doctor. Before starting brompheniramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication or other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially those for colds, hay fever, allergies, depression, seizures, muscle relaxation, pain relief (narcotics), sedation, sleep aids, tranquilizers, or vitamins. Do not take brompheniramine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, notify your healthcare provider that you are taking brompheniramine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol consumption can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this drug. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Brompheniramine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, nose, and throat, upset stomach, headache, chest congestion, and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, which require immediate medical attention, include vision problems, difficulty urinating, muscle weakness, unusual excitement (especially in children), prolonged drowsiness, dizziness, and skin rash. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store brompheniramine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share brompheniramine with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription. Brompheniramine is available in various combination products under brand names such as Allent®, Andehist® Syrup, Bromadrine PD®, Bromadrine®, Bromfed®, Bromfed-PD®, Bromfenex®, Bromfenex® PD, Bromphenirqmine-PSE®, Dallergy®-JR, Dexaphen® SA, Dimetapp® Cold & Fever, Dimetapp® Elixir, Drixoral® Allergy/Sinus, Drixoral® Cold & Allergy, Drixoral® Cold & Flu, Lodrane®, Lodrane® LD, Respahist®, Rondec® Syrup, Ultrabrom®, and Ultrabrom® PD. These products often contain additional active ingredients such as pseudoephedrine hydrochloride, acetaminophen, or dexbrompheniramine maleate.
